chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Ash'ari, from Samakah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not send any Prophet or Imam except that he is the most knowledgeable of the people regarding Allah's affairs, the best among them in executing them, and the most perceptive of them regarding the outcome of their affairs.'

He (the Prophet) said: 'And he does not command them except with what Allah commands them, nor forbids them except with what Allah forbids them, nor commands them except with what they love, nor forbids them except with what they dislike.'
He said: 'And he does not command them except with what they love, nor forbids them except with what they dislike, unless it is for their benefit, or to test them with it.'
He said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not send any Prophet except to clarify for them the truth about which they differed, and to guide them to a straight path.'

key_terms.أَمْرُ اللَّهِ: Affairs of Allah (divine commandments and matters)

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the Prophets and Imams regarding their knowledge and guidance according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this hadith within the doctrine of *Ismah* (infallibility), asserting that the Imams' alignment with divine will ensures their guidance is both authoritative and accessible to human nature. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that their commands are not arbitrary but are tailored to facilitate spiritual growth, serving as the definitive interpretation of the Quran to resolve doctrinal differences. Consequently, they act as the living proof (*Hujjah*) of Allah, guiding humanity from ambiguity to the straight path.
